For each temperature reading, update the internal temperature, use the internal helper to find the optimal speed, adjust the internal rotation speed towards it, and calculate the yield efficiency with the other helper. Return a list of yield efficiencies for each batch.

title: Glass Annealing Lehr
spec: Write a class to control a glass annealing lehr tunnel. It manages private variables for the zone temperature, glass stress level, and belt speed. It relies on internal helper methods to calculate the cooling rate based on belt speed, and to determine the residual stress relieved in the current zone based on the cooling rate. The entry function `anneal(speeds)` takes a list of belt speed settings for successive zones. For each zone, update the internal belt speed, calculate the cooling rate using the internal method, and update the internal glass stress level by subtracting the relieved stress calculated by the second helper. Return a list of residual stress levels as the glass exits each zone.

title: Seed Germination Chamber
spec: Design a class for a seed germination chamber. It maintains private state for the light status, internal moisture level, and accumulated degree days. It provides internal helper functions to calculate the daily degree days from the average temperature, and to determine if a watering cycle is needed based on the moisture level dropping below 40 percent. The entry function `germinate(temperatures)` takes a list of average daily temperatures. For each day, use the internal helper to add to the accumulated degree days, decrease the internal moisture slightly, check if watering is required using the second helper, and restore internal moisture if true. Return a list of accumulated degree days for each day.

title: Smokehouse Burner Controller
spec: Implement a class for an automated smokehouse. It keeps private variables for the internal meat temperature, smoke density, and wood chip hopper level. It features private helper methods to calculate the required burner intensity based on the meat temperature deficit, and to determine wood chip consumption based on the burner intensity and target smoke density. The entry function `smoke(readings)` accepts a list of current meat temperature readings over time. For each reading, update internal state, compute the burner intensity using the internal method, and reduce the internal hopper level by the consumption amount calculated by the other helper method. Return a list of remaining wood chip hopper levels.

title: Snowmaking Gun Controller
spec: Build a class to operate a resort snowmaking gun. It stores private state for water pressure, air pressure, and nozzle freezing risk. It requires internal helper methods to calculate the wet bulb temperature from ambient conditions, and to determine the optimal water to air ratio based on the wet bulb temperature. The entry function `snow(conditions)` takes a list of tuples containing ambient temperature and humidity. For each reading, use the internal method to find the wet bulb temperature, compute the optimal pressure ratio with the second helper, and adjust the internal water and air pressures to match this ratio. Return a list of tuples containing the adjusted water and air pressures.

title: Scuba Rebreather Monitor
spec: Create a class for a closed circuit scuba rebreather monitor. It tracks private variables for the oxygen partial pressure, diluent gas remaining, and scrubber efficiency. It includes internal helper methods to calculate the oxygen consumption rate based on depth, and to determine if a diluent flush is necessary when oxygen partial pressure spikes above 1.6 atmospheres. The entry function `monitor(depths)` accepts a list of depth readings in meters. For each reading, calculate oxygen consumption using the internal helper, update the internal oxygen partial pressure, and check if a flush is needed with the second helper, which consumes internal diluent gas and normalizes oxygen. Return a list of boolean values indicating whether a flush occurred for each reading.

title: Anesthesia Vaporizer Controller
spec: Write a class representing a medical anesthesia vaporizer. It manages private state for the liquid anesthetic volume, carrier gas flow rate, and patient weight. It uses private helper functions to calculate the required anesthetic concentration based on the patient weight, and to compute the evaporation rate based on the carrier gas flow and required concentration. The entry function `vaporize(flows)` takes a list of carrier gas flow rates adjusted by an anesthesiologist. For each adjustment, update the internal flow rate, determine the target concentration with the internal helper, calculate the liquid evaporated using the second helper, and deduct it from the internal volume. Return a list of remaining liquid volumes.

title: Neon Glass Bending Tracker
spec: Design a class that tracks the state of glass tubing for neon sign bending. It keeps private variables for the glass temperature, current bend angle, and internal gas pressure. It provides internal helper methods to calculate the pliability score from the glass temperature, and to determine the pressure loss per degree of bending. The entry function `bend(actions)` accepts a list of tuples containing a heating duration in seconds and a bend angle increment. For each action, increase internal temperature based on heating duration, calculate pliability with the internal helper, increment the internal bend angle if pliability is sufficient, and deduct pressure using the second helper. Return a list of current bend angles after each action.

title: Bounding Box Merger
spec: Implement a function `cluster(boxes)` that takes a list of four-element tuples representing the left, top, right, and bottom coordinates of text bounding boxes. The logic must find all boxes that overlap or are separated by a distance less than ten units in either dimension and combine them into a single larger bounding box enclosing all members. The process must repeat until no more boxes can be merged. Return a list of the final merged bounding box tuples sorted by their top coordinate. For example, giving a box from zero to ten and another from twelve to twenty should merge them into a single box from zero to twenty.

title: Knitting Pattern Expander
spec: Provide an entry point `expand(pattern)` that processes a string of knitting instructions consisting of plain stitches, purl stitches, and groups of stitches enclosed in parentheses followed by a multiplier. The logic must parse the string, recursively multiplying any bracketed sequences by their associated number. Track the current row length to ensure it never exceeds one hundred stitches, raising an error if it does. Output a flat list of individual stitch strings representing the full expanded row. For example, passing a purl and a group of two plain stitches multiplied by three should yield a list with one purl and six plain stitches.

title: Geocaching Route Planner
spec: Create a function `plan(caches)` that calculates an optimal sequence of visits to hidden locations represented as a list of coordinate tuples. The algorithm must start at the origin and repeatedly select the closest unvisited location until ten locations are visited or the list is exhausted. It must maintain a running total of the distance traveled, adding a fixed penalty distance of five units each time an elevation change occurs between consecutive points. Return a tuple containing the ordered list of visited coordinates and the total calculated distance. Passing three points in a straight line should return those points in order with their geometric distance.

title: Boarding Pass Parser
spec: Write a function `decode(strip)` that interprets a long string of alphanumeric characters representing a flight boarding pass. The logic must read the first two characters to determine the airline, the next four for the flight number, and then scan forward to locate a slash character dividing the passenger name fields. It must validate that the total length of the strip is exactly sixty characters, padding with spaces if necessary before processing. Output a tuple containing the airline, flight number as an integer, and the formatted passenger name. A sample string starting with two letters and four numbers followed by a name should extract those exact components.

title: Tape Recorder Simulator
spec: Develop a function `simulate(commands)` that tracks the state of a magnetic tape machine given a sequence of action strings like play, record, rewind, and stop. The tape has a maximum capacity of ninety units, and the logic must track the current spool position and the content recorded on the tape as a list of strings. Fast forwarding or rewinding moves the position by ten units per command, while playing or recording moves it by one unit per word. Return a list of strings representing the audio played back during any play commands. For example, recording three words and rewinding followed by play should output those three words.

title: Aquarium Filter Simulator
spec: Implement an entry function `filter(hours)` that models water quality in a fish tank over time. The tank starts with high levels of ammonia, nitrites, and particulate matter. The logic must step through each hour, first passing the water through a mechanical sponge that removes ten percent of particulates, then a biological medium that converts twenty percent of ammonia to nitrites and fifteen percent of nitrites to nitrates. The system must also add a small constant amount of new ammonia every hour to simulate fish waste. Return a list of three numbers representing the final concentrations of ammonia, nitrites, and nitrates. Simulating five hours should show decreased ammonia and increased nitrates.

title: Embroidery Stitch Generator
spec: Create a function `fill(outline)` that converts a list of boundary coordinate tuples into a dense sequence of zig-zag filling stitches. The logic must determine the bounding box of the shape and scan horizontally across it in steps of two units, calculating the intersections of the horizontal scan lines with the outline segments. It must generate a list of alternating left and right coordinate tuples to form a continuous zig-zag path filling the interior of the shape. Return the final list of stitch coordinates. Passing a simple square should result in a list of points alternating back and forth across its width from top to bottom.

title: Origami Crease Simulator
spec: Write a function `fold(instructions)` that models folding a square piece of paper originally spanning from zero to one hundred in both dimensions. The instructions are a list of tuples detailing a fold line starting and ending coordinates, along with a direction. The logic must mirror all current paper boundary vertices across the fold line, discarding the original points on the folded side to simulate layers stacking. After applying all folds, compute the bounding box of the resulting polygon. Output a tuple of the final width and height of the folded shape. Folding the paper exactly in half once should return a width of fifty and a height of one hundred.

title: Gear Ratio Calculator
spec: Implement `calculate(gears)` to determine the final rotation speed and direction of a clockwork mechanism. The input is a list of integers representing the number of teeth on consecutive meshed gears. The logic must iterate through the gears, maintaining the current rotational velocity and tracking the reversal of direction with each mesh. It must also handle compound gears if represented by a nested tuple of two integers, meaning they share an axle and rotate at the same speed. Return a tuple with the final gear speed as a float and an integer representing direction. Passing a ten tooth gear driving a twenty tooth gear should output half the speed in the opposite direction.

title: Sundial Shadow Projector
spec: Provide a function `cast(parameters)` that takes a tuple of latitude, day of the year, and a list of hours. The logic must calculate the sun declination angle based on the day of the year, then for each hour compute the solar altitude and azimuth angles. It must use these angles to determine the length and compass bearing of a shadow cast by a vertical stick of length ten units on a flat horizontal surface. If the sun is below the horizon, the shadow length should be recorded as zero. Return a list of tuples containing the shadow length and bearing for each hour. Midday in summer should yield a short shadow pointing north or south depending on the hemisphere.

title: Harp Pedal Adjuster
spec: Create `pluck(sequence)` to determine the exact musical notes produced by a concert harp. The harp has seven pedals corresponding to the notes of the scale, each able to be set to flat, natural, or sharp positions. The logic must maintain the state of all seven pedals and parse a sequence of commands that either change a specific pedal position or pluck a specific string. When a string is plucked, the system must apply the current pedal modifier for that note to determine the final pitch. Return a list of the modified notes played. Changing the first pedal to sharp and plucking the first string should output the sharp version of that note.

title: Braille Embosser
spec: Develop a function `emboss(text)` that translates standard characters into a layout of braille cells on a grid. The logic must parse the text, inserting a special capital indicator cell before any uppercase letters and converting numbers into a number sign cell followed by the corresponding letter cells. It must maintain a line position and automatically wrap to a new line when the horizontal limit of thirty cells is reached. Return a list of strings where each string represents a row of braille cells using a six-character binary string format for each cell. A short sentence should translate into a matching sequence of dot patterns correctly wrapped.

title: Morse Code Blinker
spec: Write an entry function `flash(message)` that converts a text string into a sequence of timing durations for a signaling lamp. The logic must map each letter to its dot and dash equivalent, then convert these into on and off time values. A dot is one time unit on, a dash is three units on, the space between parts of the same letter is one unit off, between letters is three units off, and between words is seven units off. The system must filter out unsupported punctuation before translation. Return a list of integers where positive numbers indicate duration on and negative numbers indicate duration off. The word hi should produce short positive and negative pulses separated by appropriate gaps.

title: Vinyl Groove Spacer
spec: Implement a function `cut(audio)` that calculates the radial distance of a spiral groove from the center of a record over time. The input is a list of amplitude values representing the sound volume. The logic must start at an outer radius and slowly decrease the radius with each step, increasing the step size when the amplitude is high to prevent adjacent grooves from overlapping, and keeping a minimum step size during quiet parts. It must keep track of the total rotation angle and the remaining disc space, stopping if the center label radius is reached. Return a list of radius values for each full rotation. High amplitudes should result in fewer total rotations fitting on the disc.

title: Typewriter Simulator
spec: Provide an entry point `type(keystrokes)` to process a list of character commands including normal letters, spaces, backspaces, and line feeds. The logic must maintain a virtual paper grid, tracking the current row and column of the print head. A backspace decreases the column without erasing, allowing subsequent characters to overstrike the existing ones by appending them to the grid cell. A line feed advances the row and resets the column to zero. Return a list of strings representing the final printed lines, where overstruck characters are joined together in brackets. Typing a letter, a backspace, and a different letter should yield a single position containing both letters.

title: Hot Air Balloon Controller
spec: Create a function `fly(actions)` that simulates the vertical motion of a hot air balloon given a sequence of burner blasts and vent openings. The logic must maintain internal variables for envelope temperature, ambient temperature, vertical velocity, and altitude. Burner blasts increase the envelope temperature, which generates upward buoyant acceleration, while the envelope constantly cools over time toward ambient. Venting rapidly decreases the temperature. The system must update the velocity and altitude step by step, preventing altitude from dropping below ground level. Output the maximum altitude reached during the flight. A series of long blasts should result in a high peak altitude.

title: Lighthouse Flasher
spec: Write `rotate(panels)` to model the light signature of a lighthouse seen by a distant observer. The input is a list of lens panel types that make up a circular rotating assembly, where each panel can be a bullseye lens, a colored glass pane, or a blank plate. The logic must step through time as the assembly rotates at a fixed speed, calculating when a lens sweeps past the observer line of sight to produce a bright flash, or when a colored pane changes the light hue. It must maintain the rotational angle and map it to the observer bearing. Return a list of flash events with their exact time and color. A bullseye followed by a red pane should output a white flash then a steady red light.

title: Film Projector Drive
spec: Implement `crank(milliseconds)` to trace the state of a movie projector mechanism over a given duration. The mechanism consists of a continuously rotating drive pin that engages a slotted wheel to pull the film down one frame at a time, while a rotary shutter blocks the light during the pull-down phase. The logic must calculate the angular position of the drive pin for every millisecond, determining whether the slotted wheel is stationary or moving. It must synchronize the shutter position to ensure the light is only open when the film is completely still. Return the total number of frames successfully projected. Running for one second at standard speed should output twenty four frames.

title: Sonar Echo Simulator
spec: Provide a function `sound(obstacles)` that processes a list of underwater target distances and their relative sizes. The logic must simulate a sonar pulse traveling outward at a constant speed of sound, tracking the time it takes to reach each obstacle and bounce back. It must calculate the strength of the returning echo, which degrades based on the total distance traveled and the size of the target. The system must sort the returning echoes by their arrival time and filter out any that fall below a minimum detectable threshold. Return a list of tuples containing the arrival time and echo strength. A large close target should yield a quick, strong return.

title: Kite Tension Simulator
spec: Develop an entry function `test(gusts)` that models the mechanical stress on a kite string during a windy day. The input is a sequence of wind speed values over time. The logic must track the current altitude and angle of the kite, which increase when wind speed rises and decrease during lulls. It must calculate the aerodynamic drag and lift forces at each time step, translating these into tension on the string based on its length and the kite surface area. The system must record the tension at each step and snap the string if it exceeds a critical limit. Return the highest tension recorded before the simulation ends or the string breaks. A sudden massive gust should return the breaking strain limit.

title: Boomerang Flight Simulator
spec: Create a function `throw(parameters)` that calculates the returning path of a boomerang based on initial velocity, spin rate, and wind speed. The logic must simulate the flight in discrete time steps, tracking the two dimensional coordinates, heading, and remaining rotational energy. It must apply an aerodynamic turning force that curves the heading proportionately to the current spin rate and velocity, while gradually reducing the velocity and spin due to drag. The simulation stops when the altitude hits zero. Return a list of the coordinates at each step. A proper set of inputs should produce a list of points that trace a circular path back towards the origin.

title: Yo-yo State Tracker
spec: Write an entry point `play(moves)` to track the physical state of a yo-yo during a string trick routine. The yo-yo has properties for spin speed, string wrap length, and mount state. The logic must process commands like throw, bind, mount, and dismount. A throw unwinds the string and starts the spin; a mount adds a layer of friction that slowly decreases spin speed; a bind rewinds the string only if the spin is sufficiently high. The system must validate that moves are possible from the current state, raising an error if a bind is attempted while the yo-yo is stationary. Output a string describing the final state, such as spinning on string or returned to hand.

title: Abacus Simulator
spec: Implement a function `compute(operations)` that simulates adding and subtracting numbers on a traditional bead abacus. The logic must represent the abacus as a series of columns, each tracking the position of one upper bead and four lower beads. To add or subtract, the system must parse the input numbers digit by digit, moving the required beads in each column. It must handle carry-over and borrow operations naturally by shifting beads in the adjacent higher column when a lower column overflows or underflows. After processing all operations, read the final positions of the beads. Return the resulting total as an integer. Adding five and seven should trigger a carry and result in twelve.

title: Pinball Bumper Simulator
spec: Provide an entry `launch(actions)` that tracks a ball traversing a pinball table. The table contains several stationary circular bumpers and two flippers at the bottom. The logic must update the ball position and velocity in small time steps, applying a constant downward acceleration for gravity. It must detect collisions with bumpers, which reflect the ball and add a fixed velocity boost. The input actions specify exact times when the left or right flipper is activated, which will strike the ball upward if it is within their hit zones. Return the total number of bumper hits before the ball falls below the bottom of the table. Good flipper timing should keep the ball in play and accumulate multiple hits.

title: Fountain Choreography
spec: Create `spray(sequence)` to model the arcs of water droplets shot from a programmable fountain nozzle. The input sequence defines changes to the nozzle tilt angle and water pressure at specific times. The logic must simulate the emission of a water droplet every tenth of a second, assigning it an initial velocity vector based on the current angle and pressure. It must track the parabolic trajectory of every droplet in the air, applying gravity until it hits the ground. The system must record the maximum height achieved by any droplet and the furthest horizontal distance reached. Output a tuple of these two maximum values. A high pressure vertical shot should maximize height but have zero horizontal distance.
